q.s: Who coined the term 'Indus Valley Civilisation'?
q.x: John Marshall, as Director-General of the ASI, coined the term and announced the civilisation in 1924.

q.s: The name 'Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation' stresses the sites located on which river system?
q.x: The Ghaggar–Hakra is identified with the Vedic Sarasvati; many Harappan sites lie along it.

q.s: The world's earliest known tidal dock of the Harappan period was found at:
q.x: Lothal on the Bhogava near the Gulf of Khambhat has a brick-lined dock of about 218 m x 37 m.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Gujarat?
q.x: Kalibangan is in Rajasthan on the Ghaggar; Lothal, Dholavira and Surkotada are in Gujarat.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harappan agriculture is correct?
o: Rice husk from Lothal and Rangpur is the earliest Harappan evidence of rice
A woven jute piece was found at Mohenjodaro
The earliest rice comes from Chanhudaro
Millets and rice were the staples at Mohenjodaro and Harappa
q.x: Wheat and barley were the staples at Mohenjodaro and Harappa; the woven piece was cotton.

q.s: A piece of woven cloth found at Mohenjodaro was made of:
q.x: The Harappans were among the earliest to grow cotton; a woven cotton piece was found at Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Who excavated the Amaravati stupa in 1845 and wrote 'Coins of Southern India'?
q.x: Sir Walter Elliot excavated Amaravati in 1845; Colin Mackenzie had first surveyed the site earlier.

q.s: Which foreign traveller served as Qazi of Delhi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
q.x: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, was appointed Qazi of Delhi and recorded his travels in the Rihla.

q.s: The Mudrarakshasa, which describes the rise of Chandragupta Maurya against the Nandas, was written by:
q.x: Vishakhadatta wrote the Mudrarakshasa and the Devichandraguptam.

q.s: The Devichandraguptam deals with the story of which Gupta ruler?
q.x: It tells how Chandragupta II replaced his brother Ramagupta and married Dhruvadevi.

q.s: According to the Shatapatha Brahmana, the king was linked with which deity?
q.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana gave kingship a divine basis by linking the king with Prajapati and royal sacrifices.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, which god became the supreme creator?
q.x: Indra and Agni lost their earlier pre-eminence; Prajapati became the supreme creator.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Vedic gods is NOT correct?
o: Rudra – Archer god later merged with Shiva
Pushan – Supreme creator in the Later Vedic period
q.x: In the Later Vedic period Pushan became the god of the Shudras; Prajapati was the supreme creator.

q.s: The capital of the Ikshvakus of Andhra was:
q.x: Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) was the Ikshvaku capital; Ghantasala was an ancient port.

q.s: The only 'Divya stupa' in Andhra is found at:
q.x: Adurru in East Godavari district has the only Divya stupa in Andhra.

q.s: Which of the following stupa sites is NOT associated with any event of the Buddha's life?
q.x: Bodh Gaya – enlightenment, Sarnath – first sermon, Kusinara – death; Sanchi began as Ashoka's brick stupa.

q.s: The principal social base of Jainism was formed by:
q.x: Ahimsa barred Jains from war and agriculture, so followers took to trade.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Mahamastakabhisheka of Bahubali is held every 10 years
The Vimala Vasahi temple at Mount Abu was built by Tejapala
The Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola was raised c. 981 CE by Chamundaraya
q.x: The Mahamastakabhisheka is held every 12 years; Bahubali was not a Tirthankara; Vimala Vasahi was built by Vimala Shah.

q.s: Which ancient work wrongly stated that there were no slaves in India?
q.x: Megasthenes' Indica claimed India had no slaves; the Arthashastra and Ashokan edicts mention dasas.

q.s: Under the Mauryas, the capital of Dakshinapatha was:
q.x: Ujjain was the capital of Avantipatha, Taxila of Uttarapatha, Tosali of Kalinga.

q.s: Which of the following Mauryan provinces is NOT correctly matched with its capital?
q.x: Avantipatha's capital was Ujjain; Tosali was the capital of Kalinga.

q.s: The Huna ruler Mihirakula was finally defeated by:
q.x: Yashodharman of Mandasor defeated Mihirakula c. 528 CE; Skandagupta had repulsed the earlier Huna invasions.

q.s: Ghantasala in Krishna district was known to classical writers as:
q.x: Ghantasala (Kantakasala) was Kontakossylla; Poduke is Arikamedu and Barygaza is Broach.

q.s: The weavers' guild of the Satavahana period was called:
q.x: Kolika Shreni was the weavers' guild; Tilapishaka were oil pressers.

q.s: The Harsha era began in:
q.x: Harsha ascended the throne at 16 in 606 CE, starting the Harsha era; 320 CE began the Gupta era.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harshavardhana is NOT correct?
o: He held assemblies at Kannauj and Prayag
He ascended the throne at the age of 16
He defeated Pulakesin II on the banks of the Narmada
He was a patron of Banabhatta
q.x: Harsha was defeated by Pulakesin II on the Narmada, as recorded in the Aihole inscription.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a power of Chola village assemblies?
q.x: Village assemblies owned land, raised loans and collected taxes, but minting coins was a royal prerogative.

q.s: Which Chola ruler was made co-regent in 1012 and became king in 1014?
q.x: Rajendra I was made co-regent by his father Rajaraja I in 1012.

q.s: Chola royal orders were drafted with:
o: A Tamil preamble and a Sanskrit operative part
A Sanskrit preamble and a Tamil operative part
q.x: The prashasti preamble was in Sanskrit and the operative grant in Tamil.

q.s: Malik Kafur, Alauddin Khalji's general, was called:
q.x: He was bought for 1,000 dinars, hence 'Hazar Dinari'; Ulugh Khan was Alauddin's brother.

q.s: Malik Kafur was seized at Cambay during the Gujarat campaign of 1299 by:
q.x: Nusrat Khan captured him and presented him to Alauddin.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of Alauddin Khalji's ordinances to prevent revolts?
o: Confiscating religious grants and free lands
q.x: Alauddin confiscated grants and curbed nobles; he did not make iqtas hereditary.

q.s: Under Alauddin Khalji's market control, test purchases were made through:
q.x: Alauddin sent slave boys to buy goods to check prices and weights.

q.s: The main aim of Alauddin Khalji's market control was to:
o: Pay lower wages to palace artisans
Maintain a large army on low wages
q.x: Fixed prices allowed him to pay a large army low salaries.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bilingual Arabic–Sanskrit silver coins – Mahmud of Ghazni
Completion of the Qutb Minar – Iltutmish
q.x: Din-i-Ilahi was Akbar's; the others are correctly matched.

q.s: Which ruler issued gold coins bearing the figure of Goddess Lakshmi?
q.x: Muhammad Ghori's gold coins carried Lakshmi; Mahmud issued bilingual Arabic–Sanskrit silver coins.

q.s: 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh' was written by:
q.x: Badauni wrote it; Nizamuddin Ahmad wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari; Khafi Khan wrote Muntakhab-ul-Lubab.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad.

q.s: The Charminar was built in 1591 by:
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built it in his new city Hyderabad to mark the end of a plague.

q.s: The mansabdari system had its origin in:
q.x: The decimal ranking of mansabs came from the Mongol military tradition.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mughal mansabdari system?
o: It combined civil and military duties
Mansabdars were paid in cash or jagirs
Ranks were expressed as zat and sawar
q.x: Mansabs were not hereditary; they depended on the emperor's will.

q.s: Under Babur and Humayun, the Mughal nobility was dominated by:
q.x: Akbar later added Rajputs and Hindustanis (Indian Muslims) to balance the Turanis and Iranis.

q.s: Banda Bahadur was executed at Delhi in 1716 on the orders of:
q.x: Captured at Gurdas Nangal, Banda refused to convert and was executed under Farrukhsiyar.

q.s: The city of Amritsar was founded by:
q.x: Guru Ram Das founded Amritsar; Guru Arjan built the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib).

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Nanded is associated with Guru Gobind Singh, who died there in 1708.

q.s: The Telugu 'Basava Puranam' was written by:
q.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam; he and Panditaradhya spread Veerashaivism in Andhra.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The vachanas were composed in Telugu
The Telugu Basava Puranam was written by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya
q.x: The vachanas are short Kannada sayings; Basava Puranam is by Palkuriki Somanatha.

q.s: Who collected and translated the 'Verses of Vemana' into English in 1829?
q.x: C.P. Brown, a Company official, popularised Vemana's verses.

q.s: Most of Vemana's verses are composed in which Telugu metre?
q.x: Vemana's verses are mostly in the Ataveladi metre with the refrain 'Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema'.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi was a contemporary of Alauddin Khalji
Moinuddin Chishti came with the army of Mahmud of Ghazni
Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was a contemporary of Iltutmish
Bahauddin Zakariya was a Chishti saint
q.x: Moinuddin came with Muhammad Ghori's army; Zakariya was Suhrawardi; Chiragh-i-Delhi lived under the Tughlaqs.

q.s: Bahauddin Zakariya, a contemporary of Iltutmish, belonged to which Sufi order?
q.x: Bahauddin Zakariya founded the Suhrawardi order in India at Multan.

q.s: In Shivaji's Ashtapradhan, the minister in charge of finance (treasury and accounts) was the:
q.x: Amatya (Majumdar) – finance; Sachiv (Surnis) – correspondence; Sumant – foreign affairs; Panditrao – religious affairs.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Shivaji's Ashtapradhan is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Sachiv (Surnis) handled royal correspondence; finance was the Amatya's.

q.s: 'Chauth', levied by the Marathas on territories outside their direct rule, was:
q.x: Chauth (one-fourth) was the price of being spared Maratha raids; Sardeshmukhi was an extra 10 per cent.

q.s: The 'cartaz' system introduced by the Portuguese in Indian waters was a:
q.x: Begun by Vasco da Gama in 1502 and systematised by Albuquerque; ships without it were seized.

q.s: Who was the first envoy of James I to reach the court of Jahangir?
q.x: Hawkins reached Jahangir's court in 1608; Roe came in 1615; Terry was Roe's chaplain.

q.s: Ralph Fitch, the English traveller of 1583–86, visited the court of:
q.x: Ralph Fitch was among the first Englishmen to travel in India, in Akbar's time.

q.s: By which Mughal emperor's Farman of 1717 did the English Company get duty-free trade in Bengal for Rs 3,000 a year?
q.x: The 1717 Farman, called the Magna Carta of the Company, was granted by Farrukhsiyar.

q.s: Child's War (1686–90) was fought by the English East India Company against:
q.x: The Company was defeated and pardoned on payment of a fine.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: In 1856 Dalhousie announced that the Mughal successors would lose the imperial title
The titles of the Carnatic Nawab and the Tanjore Raja were abolished in 1848
Nana Saheb was the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao I
In 1849 Dalhousie announced that Bahadur Shah's successors would have to leave the Red Fort
q.x: The 1856 announcement was Canning's; the titles were abolished in 1855; Nana Saheb was Baji Rao II's adopted son.

q.s: Nana Saheb's grievance before 1857 was the denial of the pension of his adoptive father:
q.x: Baji Rao II, the last Peshwa, had adopted Nana Saheb; Dalhousie refused to continue the pension.

q.s: Who called the loyal princes 'breakwaters to the storm' during the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: Canning, who also read Queen Victoria's Proclamation at Allahabad in 1858.

q.s: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1858 withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse
Canning read Queen Victoria's Proclamation at Allahabad
Rani Chennamma of Kittur fought against Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse
After 1858 the princes were guaranteed their states
q.x: Rani Chennamma fought the British in 1824, long before Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse (1848).

q.s: Which of the following pairs (book – author) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wheel of History – Ram Manohar Lohia
Problems of the Far East – Curzon
q.x: 'The Untold Story' was written by Lt Gen B.M. Kaul.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a reason for the failure of the Revolt of 1857?
o: Lack of unity among rebel leaders
Superior British weapons like the Enfield rifle
British use of the electric telegraph
The Madras Presidency joining the rebels
q.x: The Madras Presidency stayed largely quiet; the telegraph and Enfield rifle helped the British.

q.s: Muzaffar Jang was killed in 1751 at:
q.x: He was killed at Rayachoti; Bussy then installed Salabat Jang, fourth son of Nizam-ul-Mulk.

q.s: During the Second Carnatic War, Salabat Jang was installed as Nizam by:
q.x: The French general Bussy placed Salabat Jang on the throne.

q.s: Awadh was annexed by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 on the ground of:
q.x: Awadh and Coorg were annexed for misgovernance; Sindh and Punjab by conquest.

q.s: Which of the following territories was NOT annexed by the British by conquest?
q.x: Coorg (1834), like Awadh (1856), was annexed on the ground of misgovernance.

q.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal, who was the Naib Diwan for Bengal?
q.x: Reza Khan was Naib Diwan for Bengal and Shitab Rai for Bihar.

q.s: The Dual Government in Bengal was abolished in 1772 by:
q.x: Hastings ended the system Clive had set up in 1765.

q.s: The Indian Universities Act was passed in 1904 under:
q.x: It followed the Raleigh Universities Commission of 1902.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Lord Curzon?
o: Annulment of the Partition of Bengal
Creation of the North-West Frontier Province
q.x: The Partition was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge II.

q.s: Fort William College at Calcutta was set up in 1800 by:
q.x: Wellesley set it up to train civil servants; Haileybury replaced it in 1806.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Haileybury replaced Fort William College for training in 1806.

q.s: Which Charter Act introduced open competition for the Indian civil services?
q.x: The 1853 Act, the last Charter Act, ended the Directors' patronage.

q.s: Which of the following about the Charter Act of 1853 is NOT correct?
o: It was the last Charter Act
It renewed the Company's rule for a further 20 years
It added new legislative members to the Governor-General's Council
It separated the legislative and executive functions of the Council
q.x: The 1853 Act renewed Company rule with no fixed term.

q.s: The Ceded Districts – Bellary, Anantapur, Cuddapah and Kurnool – were ceded to the British in 1800 by:
q.x: They were ceded by the Nizam under the Subsidiary Alliance.

q.s: Thomas Munro, the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts, died of cholera in 1827 at:
q.x: He died at Pattikonda and was buried at Gooty.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Indian Press Act, 1910 was passed under Lord Curzon
The Vernacular Press Act was repealed in 1882 by Lord Ripon
Section 124A was added to the IPC under Lord Lytton
On repeal of the Act, the pre-censorship clause was retained
q.x: The pre-censorship clause was dropped; 124A came in 1870 under Lord Mayo; the 1910 Act was under Minto II.

q.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta was set up under:
q.x: Set up in 1774 under the Regulating Act with Elijah Impey as Chief Justice.

q.s: Under the Cornwallis Code of 1793, the Collector:
o: Was made head of the Sadar Diwani Adalat
q.x: The Cornwallis Code separated revenue and judicial work and created the post of District Judge.

q.s: The Indian Penal Code came into being in:
q.x: The CPC came in 1859, the IPC in 1860 and the Presidency High Courts in 1862.

q.s: Which of the following High Courts was NOT set up in 1862?
q.x: The Allahabad High Court (first at Agra) was set up in 1866.

q.s: The Peel Commission on the army was set up in:
q.x: The Peel Commission recommended a higher share of European troops after 1857.

q.s: Raja Rammohan Roy was given the title 'Raja' by:
q.x: Mughal emperor Akbar II sent him to England as his envoy; he died at Bristol in 1833.

q.s: The title 'Maharishi' is associated with:
q.x: Debendranath Tagore led the Brahmo Samaj after Roy and was known as Maharishi.

q.s: Which of the following statements about M.G. Ranade is correct?
o: He was associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
He founded the Deccan Education Society with Tilak
He founded the Widow Remarriage Association at Calcutta
He held that social reform should wait until political freedom
q.x: Ranade was linked to the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870); the Widow Remarriage Association (1861) was in Bombay; postponing social reform was Tilak's view.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mahar community
Savitribai Phule headed the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj
Phule's girls' school of 1848 was at Bombay
q.x: Phule was a Mali; the school was at Pune; the title 'Mahatma' came in 1888.

q.s: Jyotiba Phule founded which organisation in 1873?
q.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) fought caste discrimination; Savitribai headed its women's section.

q.s: Gurajada Appa Rao's play 'Kanyasulkam' attacked the practice of:
q.x: Kanyasulkam ('bride price') satirised the sale of young girls in marriage.

q.s: In 'Kanyasulkam', Madhuravani is portrayed as a:
q.x: Girisham is the educated fraud and Buchamma the widow.

q.s: The Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910), regarded as the first all-India women's body, was founded by:
q.x: Sarala Devi founded it; its first session was at Allahabad.

q.s: The Rajah-Moonje Pact of 1932 on reserved seats in joint electorates was signed by M.C. Rajah and:
q.x: It was a forerunner of the Poona Pact (September 1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar.

q.s: 'Mooknayak' (1920), the first journal of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, means:
q.x: Mooknayak (1920) was followed by Bahishkrit Bharat (1927) and Janata (1930).

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Ambedkar's journal – year) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Bahishkrit Bharat was started in 1927.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a programme of the Swadeshi movement against the Partition of Bengal?
q.x: Non-cooperation was the programme of 1920.

q.s: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti of Barisal was led by:
q.x: Ashwini Kumar Dutt built a strong mass movement at Barisal.

q.s: Who said that the announcement of the Partition of Bengal 'fell like a bombshell'?
q.x: Banerjea, with K.K. Mitra, led the anti-partition agitation.

q.s: 'Bengal united is a power; Bengal divided will pull in several different ways' was said by:
q.x: Home Secretary H.H. Risley's note revealed the political motive of the partition.

q.s: The official justification given for the Partition of Bengal (1905) was:
q.x: The real motive was to weaken Bengali nationalism and divide Hindus and Muslims.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio?
q.x: Aurobindo was an Extremist leader of Bengal but not one of Lal-Bal-Pal.

q.s: With Lala Lajpat Rai, who led the Extremists of Punjab?
q.x: Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh (Bhagat Singh's uncle) were deported in 1907.

q.s: The first Home Rule League, started in April 1916, was founded by:
q.x: Tilak's League began in April 1916; Annie Besant's at Madras in September 1916. The movement faded after the Montford reforms (1918).

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Chandrashekhar Azad was born at Bhavra in present Madhya Pradesh
Rajguru was born at Banga in Lyallpur district
Azad died at Alfred Park on 23 March 1931
Sukhdev taught at the Kashi Vidyapith
q.x: Azad died on 27 February 1931; Banga was Bhagat Singh's birthplace; Sukhdev taught at the National College, Lahore.

q.s: Rajguru, who was hanged with Bhagat Singh, was born at:
q.x: Banga was Bhagat Singh's birthplace; Bhavra was Azad's.

q.s: Who were hanged along with Bhagat Singh on 23 March 1931?
q.x: Batukeshwar Dutt got transportation for life in the Assembly bomb case; Jatin Das died on hunger strike in 1929.

q.s: The Moplah rebellion of 1921 took place in:
q.x: Led by Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar, it was against jenmi landlords and the British.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Moplah rebellion of 1921?
q.x: K. Kelappan led the Guruvayur temple entry satyagraha.

q.s: The Sanyasi Revolt broke out in Bengal following:
q.x: The Bengal famine of 1770 and Company exactions triggered the revolt.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the Gandhian phase of peasant movements?
q.x: The Pabna agrarian league (1873) belongs to the pre-Gandhian phase.

q.s: Lala Lajpat Rai, who died after the police lathi charge during the Simon Commission protest at Lahore, had presided over the first session of the:
q.x: Lajpat Rai presided over the first AITUC session in 1920 at Bombay.

q.s: The Hunter Committee set up after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre was officially named:
q.x: Announced on 14 October 1919; the Congress set up its own non-official inquiry.

q.s: The Nagpur session of the Congress (1920) fixed the membership fee at:
q.x: It also set up a Working Committee of 15 and linguistic Provincial Congress Committees.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a decision of the Nagpur session of the Congress (1920)?
o: Adoption of Purna Swaraj as the goal
Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines
q.x: Purna Swaraj was adopted at the Lahore session of 1929.

q.s: Subhas Chandra Bose regarded whom as his political guru?
q.x: Bose resigned from the ICS in 1921 and worked under C.R. Das.

q.s: Part 1 of Subhas Bose's 'The Indian Struggle' was written in exile at:
q.x: It was published in London in 1935 and banned in India.

q.s: The motto of the Indian National Army was:
q.x: Unity, Faith, Sacrifice; 'Dilli Chalo' was its battle cry.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a brigade/regiment of the Indian National Army?
q.x: The INA had Subhash, Gandhi, Azad and Nehru brigades and the Rani Jhansi Regiment.

q.s: Gandhi's first satyagraha in South Africa (1906) was against:
q.x: The 1906 Transvaal ordinance required Indians to register; the poll tax struggle came in 1913.

q.s: The £3 poll tax on Indians in South Africa was abolished by:
q.x: The Gandhi–Smuts agreement led to the Indian Relief Act of 1914.

q.s: Who was the only Telugu participant in Gandhi's Dandi March?
q.x: Yerneni Subrahmanyam of Krishna district later founded an ashram at Komaravolu.

q.s: During the Salt Satyagraha, Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi was arrested at:
q.x: She joined Rajagopalachari's salt march to Vedaranyam and was the first woman arrested in Madras Presidency.

q.s: 'Feathers and Stones', a prison diary, was written by:
q.x: He also wrote the 'History of the Indian National Congress'.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT founded by Pattabhi Sitaramayya?
q.x: Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Andhra Pradesh schemes is NOT correctly matched?
o: Janmabhoomi – Health insurance for the poor
Rajiv Aarogyasri – Health insurance for the poor
Fee Reimbursement – Higher education of poor students
q.x: Janmabhoomi (1997) was about people's participation in development.

q.s: The 'Gentlemen's Agreement' between the leaders of Andhra and Telangana was signed on:
q.x: It preceded the SR Act (31 August 1956) and the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956.

q.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Hyderabad State who worked to allay Telangana's fears about the merger?
q.x: Burgula, on the High Command's direction, supported Visalandhra.

q.s: The Zonal Councils were set up under:
q.x: They are statutory bodies under Part III of the SR Act.

q.s: Who is the Chairman of each Zonal Council?
q.x: The Vice-Chairman is a Chief Minister by rotation.

q.s: The capital of Andhra State (1953–56) was:
q.x: Andhra State's first Chief Minister was Tanguturi Prakasam.

q.s: The Andhra–Madras border on the formation of Andhra State was fixed by the:
q.x: The Wanchoo Committee studied financial and administrative problems of forming the state.

q.s: Who was the first Dalit Chief Minister in India?
q.x: Sanjivayya was CM of Andhra Pradesh (1960–62) and later AICC President.

q.s: Which leader from Andhra Pradesh became President of India in 1977?
q.x: He had earlier been AICC President (1960) and Lok Sabha Speaker; V.V. Giri became President in 1969.

q.s: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme in Andhra Pradesh was launched in 1983 by:
q.x: The scheme began on 14 April 1983.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of N.T. Rama Rao's government?
q.x: NTR abolished the Legislative Council in 1985; it was revived in 2007.

q.s: The Five-Point Formula of 1972 on the Mulki rules was announced by:
q.x: Announced on 27 November 1972; it was replaced by the Six-Point Formula of 1973.

q.s: The Nasik Prashasti praising Gautamiputra Satakarni was issued by:
q.x: His mother Gautami Balashri called him the destroyer of Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.

q.s: Ushavadatta, whose inscriptions are found at Nasik and Karle, was the son-in-law of:
q.x: Ushavadatta, son-in-law of the Kshaharata ruler Nahapana, deposited money with weavers' guilds.

q.s: In the Nasik Prashasti, the region 'Vidarbha' refers to:
q.x: Suratha was Saurashtra and Akara was East Malwa (Vidisha).
